newsitem.title: UK: IGC raises 1996 wheat output, trims stocks.
newsitem.headline: IGC raises 1996 wheat output, trims stocks.

text.p: The International Grains Council (IGC) on Tuesday raised its estimate for world wheat production in 1996 by two million tonnes to 575 million tonnes mainly due to better crops in Australia and Argentina.

In its latest monthly report, the IGC raised world wheat consumption by six million tonnes from its previous estimate to 569 million tonnes and trimmed the end-season stocks (1996/97) to 102 million tonnes from last month's forecast of 104 million.
The stocks were at their lowest since 1979, with the exception of the 20-year low of 95 million tonnes in 1995/96 which followed the 1995 crop estimated of 541 million tonnes.
Production in Argentina was put one million tonnes higher at a record 15.5 million tonnes for 1996 while Australian output was increased to 21 million tonnes from 20.2 million tonnes.

"The crop estimate for Argentine has been increased...after recent reports of higher than expected yields due to excellent growing conditions. Planted area is believed to have been increased by about 39 percent to around 6.8 million hectares," the IGC said.
Australia was expected to achieve above average yields but wet conditions in parts of Victoria, New South Wales and central Queensland could lead to lower wheat quality.

China's production was also set at a higher 108 million tonnes from the previous 107 million tonnes following reports of better yields. But the forecast for India was reduced by one million tonnes to 63 million tonnes.
In the former Soviet Union, the estimate for Ukraine was lowered slightly due to the worst weather conditions for 50 years.

The IGC said combined carryover stocks in the five major exporting counties -- Australia, Argentina, United States, Canada and the EU -- were forecast at 40 million tonnes, the same as last month and up from 28 million last season with most of the increase being in Australia and the EU.
